introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in this question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One (booklet 0000/0595/3/Grp 1), Group Three (Grp 3) and Group Four (Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Group One: Task I (word processing, 15 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (HTML, 15 marks). Group Three: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 15 marks), Task 3 (HTML, 15 marks). Group Four: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (C or Pascal program, 10 marks). Each group is worth 50 marks.

The working files named in the tasks (pictures, logo, signature) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Launch the spreadsheet on your computer and enter the information given above. *[4 marks]*

Data to key in (cells A1 to I8, plus the two labels):

| A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | I |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No | Name | Test 1 | Test 2 | Tests Total | Exam | Term Total | Rank | Remarks |
| 1 | Thelma | 10 | 9 | | 15 | | | |
| 2 | Peter | 11 | 5 | | 9 | | | |
| 3 | Henry | 9 | 12 | | 12 | | | |
| 4 | Joan | 14 | 13 | | 9 | | | |
| 5 | Paul | 5 | 6 | | 9 | | | |
| 6 | Audrey | 3 | 9 | | 10 | | | |
| 7 | Mispa | 11 | 11 | | 7 | | | |

| Cell | Content |
|---|---|
| E10 | Count Failed |
| E11 | Count Passed |
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open the spreadsheet program (for example *Microsoft Excel* or *LibreOffice Calc*) and start a new workbook. Click the cell **A1** and key in the data row by row, using **Tab** to move to the next cell on the right and **Enter** to go to the next row.

1. Row 1: the headings **No, Name, Test 1, Test 2, Tests Total, Exam, Term Total, Rank, Remarks**.
2. Rows 2 to 8: the serial numbers 1 to 7, the names (Thelma, Peter, Henry, Joan, Paul, Audrey, Mispa), and the scores of Test 1, Test 2 and Exam as **numbers** (so that they can be used in formulas). Leave E, G, H and I empty: they will receive formulas.
3. Cells **E10** and **E11**: the labels *Count Failed* and *Count Passed*.
4. Check every number against the question (one wrong digit gives wrong results later).

Marking idea (4 marks, indicative): spreadsheet launched (1); headings and names correct (1); all the scores correct (1); the two labels in place (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: b) In cell E2, calculate the sum of Test 1 and Test 2 on 20. Use the formula $\frac{2}{3}$(Test 1 + Test 2). *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each test is marked out of 15, so the two tests together are out of 30; multiplying by two thirds brings the total back to a mark out of 20 (30 x 2/3 = 20).

In **E2** type

**`=2/3*(C2+D2)`**

and press Enter. The brackets are essential: without them, only D2 would be multiplied by 2/3.

Check for Thelma: 2/3 x (10 + 9) = 2/3 x 19 = 12.67 (rounded to 2 decimal places, shown in the cell as 12.67).

Marking idea (2 marks): formula starts with = and uses the cells C2 and D2 (1); the factor 2/3 and the brackets are correct (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Copy the formula to Cells E3:E8. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **E2**, then drag the fill handle (the small square at the bottom right corner of the cell) down to **E8** (or copy E2, select E3:E8 and paste). The references are **relative**, so each row uses its own scores.

Results (Tests Total on 20), computed by script from the data:

| Row | Name | Test 1 | Test 2 | Tests Total (E) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 10 | 9 | 12.67 |
| 3 | Peter | 11 | 5 | 10.67 |
| 4 | Henry | 9 | 12 | 14.00 |
| 5 | Joan | 14 | 13 | 18.00 |
| 6 | Paul | 5 | 6 | 7.33 |
| 7 | Audrey | 3 | 9 | 8.00 |
| 8 | Mispa | 11 | 11 | 14.67 |

Marking idea (1 mark): formula copied to E3:E8 with correct values.

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Write in the space below, the formula you find in Cell E8, after copying as requested in (b) above. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the formula of E2 is copied six rows down, each row number in the references increases by 6 (relative references: 2 becomes 8). The formula found in **E8** is therefore

**`=2/3*(C8+D8)`**

Check with Mispa: 2/3 x (11 + 11) = 2/3 x 22 = 14.67.

questions.enonce_markdown: d) In column G, calculate the total scores on 20 for all the students (each score in Column G is the average of the corresponding scores in Columns E and F). *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Term Total is the average of the Tests Total (column E) and the Exam score (column F), which are both out of 20.

In **G2** type **`=AVERAGE(E2,F2)`** (or `=(E2+F2)/2`, or `=AVERAGE(E2:F2)`, which gives the same result because E and F are next to each other) and copy it down to **G8**.

Results:

| Row | Name | Tests Total (E) | Exam (F) | Term Total (G) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 12.67 | 15 | 13.83 |
| 3 | Peter | 10.67 | 9 | 9.83 |
| 4 | Henry | 14.00 | 12 | 13.00 |
| 5 | Joan | 18.00 | 9 | 13.50 |
| 6 | Paul | 7.33 | 9 | 8.17 |
| 7 | Audrey | 8.00 | 10 | 9.00 |
| 8 | Mispa | 14.67 | 7 | 10.83 |

Check for Thelma: (12.67 + 15) / 2 = 13.83. The values in column G are recalculated with Python from the data of the question.

Marking idea (2 marks): correct formula in G2 (1); copied to G8 with correct values (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: e) In Column H, compute the rank of each student based on the scores in Column G. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the **RANK** function: in **H2** type

**`=RANK(G2,$G$2:$G$8)`**

then copy it down to **H8**. The first argument is the score to rank; the second argument is the list of all the Term Totals, fixed with dollar signs (absolute reference) so that the list does not move when the formula is copied. The largest score gets rank 1 (default order: descending).

Results:

| Row | Name | Term Total (G) | Rank (H) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 13.83 | 1 |
| 3 | Peter | 9.83 | 5 |
| 4 | Henry | 13.00 | 3 |
| 5 | Joan | 13.50 | 2 |
| 6 | Paul | 8.17 | 7 |
| 7 | Audrey | 9.00 | 6 |
| 8 | Mispa | 10.83 | 4 |

Without the dollar signs, the list would shift down at each row and the ranks would be wrong.

Marking idea (1 mark): RANK used with the whole list G2:G8 correctly fixed.

questions.enonce_markdown: f) Write the name of the student who is ranked first in the space below. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The student with rank 1 is the one with the highest Term Total, 13.83: **Thelma** (second is Joan with 13.50).

questions.enonce_markdown: g) In cell I2 use the IF function to display the word "PASSED" if the Term Total is greater than or equal to 10, and the word "FAILED" otherwise. Copy the function to Cells I3 to I8. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **I2** type

**`=IF(G2>=10,"PASSED","FAILED")`**

and copy it down. Reading of the function: IF(test, value if the test is true, value if the test is false). The words are text, so they are written between double quotation marks; the test is G2 greater than or equal to 10 (`>=`).

Results (the formula logic was run in Python on the data):

| Row | Name | Term Total (G) | Remarks (I) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Thelma | 13.83 | PASSED |
| 3 | Peter | 9.83 | FAILED |
| 4 | Henry | 13.00 | PASSED |
| 5 | Joan | 13.50 | PASSED |
| 6 | Paul | 8.17 | FAILED |
| 7 | Audrey | 9.00 | FAILED |
| 8 | Mispa | 10.83 | PASSED |

Peter (9.83), Paul (8.17) and Audrey (9.00) are below 10 and FAIL; the other four students pass.

Marking idea (4 marks, indicative): IF function with the test G2>=10 (2); the two words correctly written (1); copied down with correct results (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: h) In Cells G10 and G11, use the COUNTIF function to compute the number of failed and passed cases based on the values in cells G2:G8. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The function **COUNTIF(range, criterion)** counts the cells of a range that satisfy a criterion. The criterion is written between double quotation marks when it contains a comparison sign.

- **G10** (Count Failed): **`=COUNTIF(G2:G8,"<10")`** gives **3** (Peter 9.83, Paul 8.17 and Audrey 9.00).
- **G11** (Count Passed): **`=COUNTIF(G2:G8,">=10")`** gives **4** (Thelma, Henry, Joan and Mispa).

Check: 3 + 4 = 7, the number of students. (The same counts can also be obtained with `=COUNTIF(I2:I8,"FAILED")` and `=COUNTIF(I2:I8,"PASSED")`, but the question asks for the values of G2:G8.)

Marking idea (4 marks, indicative): COUNTIF with the range G2:G8 (1 + 1); correct criteria "<10" and ">=10" (1 + 1).
